subject: Combing density estimates and SE, lcl, ucl

messages.author: a9c909c7586d903d
messages.subject: Combing density estimates and SE, lcl, ucl
parts:
Hello secr users,

We are running series of simulations to assess the effect of modelling (and failing to model) sex and spatial variation in SECR parameter estimates on density estimates. We have 2 trap arrays within 3 unique study areas (each array samples distinct populations), where parameters (D, g0, sigma) vary for each area and sex. We are using a multi-session capthist object (with a total of 12 sessions- 2 traplines x male and female x 3 areas) fit using full likelihood (as we are interested in modeling density covariates in the future we are not using conditional likelihood). sessioncov is used to model the effects of both sex and area. We are aware that sex can also be modelled using either individual covariates or groups. Everything is run on secr v 4.3.1.  

The challenge we are having is estimating total density (for both sexes by area) and it’s SE, ucl and lcl using predict, which, by default, presents 12 session-specific estimates. We would prefer to present estimates of total density (both sexes) within study areas, but have not been able to using the newdata argument. Similarly, we were unable to achieve this using derived and the groups argument (which seems to be consistent with the documentation – if using fully likelihood models using g (groups) will not be handled correctly?).  

Any suggestions are much appreciated.

Thank you in advance,

Brynn

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Combing density estimates and SE, lcl, ucl
parts:
Hello Brynn
I think you can tackle this by controlling how factor covariates are coded with the details option 'contrasts'. There are some relevant notes in Section 7.8 of https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/openCR-vignette.pdf. The idea is to code the covariate so that one beta parameter corresponds to the mean (but note caveat in Section 7.8). The same option is available in 'secr'. Example below (replace 'session' with 'sex' in your case).
Murray

library(secr)
msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCHp[[1]]), buffer = 250, nx = 25)
setNumThreads(7)
fit <-secr.fit(ovenCHp,model = D~session, details =
        list(contrasts = list(session = contr.sum)))
# extract
meanD <- exp(coef(fit)['D',c('beta','lcl','ucl')])
est <- do.call(rbind, lapply(predict(fit),'[',1,))
# plot
par(mar=c(4,5,2,2))
plot(2005:2009, est$estimate, ylim=c(0,3), pch=16, xlab='',
    ylab= expression(paste('Density', ~~ha^-1)))
segments(2005:2009, est$lcl, 2005:2009, est$ucl)
abline(h=meanD, lty=c(1,2,2), col='red')

Hello Murray, 

Thank you for the quick response. For now we may avoid using the 'contrasts' method to avoid having to re-fit all the models. However, thank you for the suggestion- we will keep this option in mind moving forward. 

Cheers, 
Brynn
